chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Abi al-Jawza' from al-Husayn b. Ilwan from Amr b. Khalid from Asim b. Abi al-Nujud al-Asadi from Ibn Umar from al-Hasan b. Ali (peace be upon them both). He said: I heard my father Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

If a Muslim person were to sit in his place of prayer in which he prays Fajr, remembering Allah the Mighty and Majestic until sunrise, he will have the reward of one who has made pilgrimage to the House of Allah, and he will be forgiven. If he sits in it until the moment in which prayer becomes permissible again after sunrise, then prays two or four units, all his past sins will be forgiven, and he will have the reward of one who has made pilgrimage to the House of Allah.

key_terms.حاج بيت الله: Pilgrim to the House of Allah: one who performs Hajj to the Ka'ba in Mecca
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic (Azz wa Jall): divine attributes emphasizing Allah's power and glory
key_terms.مصلاه: His place of prayer (musalla): the spot where one regularly performs prayers

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of sitting in the prayer place after Fajr until sunrise in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet (s), as narrated through Imam al-Hasan from Imam Ali (as), teaches that a Muslim who remains in his place of prayer after Fajr, engaged in the remembrance of Allah until sunrise, receives the reward equivalent to performing Hajj and is granted forgiveness. If he continues sitting until the time of the post-sunrise prayer (Ishraq) and prays two or four units, all his previous sins are forgiven and he again receives the reward of Hajj. This hadith, delivered in Rajab 368 AH, demonstrates how accessible spiritual rewards can be through simple acts of devotion.
